edits.html:
Management Groin pain, lost internal rotation and a widened, irregular physis mean SCFE (slipped capital femoral epiphysis), even before the epiphysis visibly displaces. Treatment is in situ screw fixation across the physis, with the child non-weight-bearing until surgery. Bracing, casting, traction and physical therapy do not stop the slip. When the slip may be unstable, a cross-table lateral view avoids forcing the hip into the frog-leg position.
How NBME framed it The lead-in granted analgesia and weight-loss counseling, and the stem showed only a widened, irregular physis, never naming a slip. The options were a treatment-of-a-mimic menu: bracing and casting treat developmental dysplasia of the hip, traction treats a fracture, and physical therapy treats a strain.
edits.note: Q6: management of SCFE (pre-slip, in situ fixation, what does not work) and NBME framing

edits.html:
True-fact-wrong-slotPhysical therapy: tempting for weeks of hip pain and stiffness in an overweight teenager (limited motion without fever); it treats a strain after an injury, and there was no injury here.
True-fact-wrong-slotAbduction bracing: tempting as a real hip treatment (limited abduction); it treats developmental dysplasia of the hip in infants, and this is a 13-year-old with a widened physis.
True-fact-wrong-slotTraction: tempting as a reflex for a painful hip and a limp (a groin injury picture); it restores length after a displaced fracture, and there was no trauma or fracture.
True-fact-wrong-slotSpica cast immobilization: tempting as another way to hold the hip still (it was once used for this slip); it holds an infant hip reduced for developmental dysplasia, and casting a slip was abandoned because of chondrolysis.
edits.note: Q6: one trapline per NBME distractor

edits.stem: 13-year-old boy above the 97th percentile for BMI with 4 weeks of intermittent left groin pain and a limp, no fever; left hip internal rotation and abduction are limited, and the hip externally rotates on passive flexion; AP and cross-table lateral films show an irregular, widened left femoral physis with mild osteopenia of the femoral head and neck
edits.companion: pinning in situ across the physis stops further slipping
edits.lead_in: In addition to analgesia and weight-loss counseling, which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

edits.stem: 12-year-old girl with 3 weeks of thigh pain who now cannot bear weight on the right leg after a minor fall; radiographs show the right femoral epiphysis displaced off the neck
edits.answer: Forceful closed reduction of the slip
edits.companion: forcing the epiphysis back raises the risk of avascular necrosis; pin it where it lies
